article_title: GW Explorer: A Beginner's Guide -- Developing a Computational Gravitational-Wave Outreach Curriculum for High School Students
citation: Rachel Langgin, Bradlee Tejeda and Carl-Johan Haster. (2026). GW Explorer: A Beginner's Guide –– Developing a Computational Gravitational-Wave Outreach Curriculum for High School Students. https://github.com/rlanggin/GW_Explorer_A_Beginners_Guide
title: GW Explorer: A Beginner's Guide — three-notebook computational curriculum with released GitHub materials
description: GW Explorer is a curriculum of Python Jupyter notebooks that "weave together narrative explanations, interactive visualizations, guided questions, and executable code". Notebook 1 covers GW foundations with an embedded Python tutorial; Notebook 2 covers binary merger waveform simulation; Notebook 3 introduces "simplified Bayesian inference concepts". Materials are publicly released at https://github.com/rlanggin/GW_Explorer_A_Beginners_Guide and mirror at rachellanggin.com/tutorials.
requirements: Students need a browser-based environment such as Google Colab; the notebooks were tested to work as standalone, self-guided instructional materials.
constraints: The authors state the Bayesian parameter-estimation content is presented "at a simplified level" relative to research practice.
target_learning_goals: computational literacy and basic Python programming
examples: Notebook sliders let students adjust component masses and luminosity distance, updating waveforms in real time as they visualize how variables affect signal amplitude and phase.

title: Pair accessible computational notebooks with near-peer graduate-student mentors to lower barriers for novice programmers
description: The article pairs its notebooks with "graduate volunteers who serve as near-peer mentors, offering real-time guidance through unfamiliar computational and physical terrain". Mentors received short training on notebook content, common misconceptions, and coding-error troubleshooting, then provided individualized help during workshops. The authors report this combination allowed engagement "regardless of where they started".
requirements: Mentors need a short training session covering notebook content, common student misconceptions, and troubleshooting for typical coding errors.
constraints: The article notes the workshop format introduces variability in mentor interactions and classroom pacing that can be difficult to maintain compared to self-guided instruction.
target_learners: high school students with no prior coding experience
examples: UNLV graduate mentors guided Las Vegas Academy students through notebook activities, answered career-pathway questions, and connected students with college application materials.

title: Scaffolded progressive notebook sequence moving from foundational physics to authentic data-analysis workflows
description: The curriculum is "built as a progressive sequence of computational Jupyter notebooks that guide students from foundational GW physics to simplified yet authentic data analysis workflows". Each notebook combines narrative, executable code, guided exercises, and interactive plotting. "The scaffolded structure is intentional as students build enough conceptual and computational footing in early notebooks to engage meaningfully with GW data by the end of the sequence."
requirements: Each notebook must weave narrative explanations, executable Python code, guided exercises, and interactive plotting in a unified environment.
examples: The sequence runs Notebook 1 (GW foundations with Python tutorial), Notebook 2 (binary merger waveform simulation), Notebook 3 (parameter estimation basics).
